headline: High: Replit Agent’s broad shell/files/network defaults can conflict with a read-only docs hub, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by ai-engineering-hub’s lack of runtime surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs/repo hub with no runtime I/O surfaces, while Profile B can read/write Repl files and act on them. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A’s content is copied into B’s workspace, B could misread instructions from untrusted text. The pairwise bridge is therefore manual and limited.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is copied into agent_b workspace files, THEN agent_b may parse it as instructions.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-execute file-derived prompts, THEN prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs in a separate notes file, not in agent_b workspace.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data.
Disable any auto-run or auto-parse step for workspace files.
Review copied snippets before pasting into agent_b.
Use a read-only staging folder for agent_a artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, while Agent B touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration with broad network egress. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, so leakage is not default. Risk appears only if sensitive Replit data is manually transferred into A or if A is extended with file access.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are copied from agent_b into agent_a, THEN those contents may be exposed in downstream outputs.
IF agent_a is later granted filesystem or network access, THEN leakage risk increases materially.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into agent_a prompts.
Redact deployment config before sharing with agent_a.
Keep agent_b secrets in Replit Secrets only.
Audit any exported text from agent_a before reuse.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on copied artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent B can write the Repl filesystem and modify git state, but the pair lacks a shared writable surface or locking mechanism. The only plausible conflict is indirect if A’s docs are manually mirrored into B’s workspace, which is unusual.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are manually copied into the same Repl directory that agent_b edits, THEN file-level conflicts can occur.
IF multiple agent_b instances edit the same Repl filesystem concurrently, THEN git or file conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Keep agent_a artifacts outside the Repl workspace.
Use one writer at a time for agent_b.
Commit frequently to reduce merge scope.
Lock shared files before edits.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a docs hub and can produce guidance, while Agent B is an action-capable coding agent. The pair can cascade if B treats A’s text as authoritative, but A has no execution authority and B’s tool use is checkpointed. That makes the pathway plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of truth without verification, THEN incorrect guidance can propagate into code or shell actions.
IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts, THEN B may act on stale or misleading instructions.
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources before acting.
Ask B to summarize uncertainties before execution.
Separate drafting from execution steps.
Mark A outputs as advisory only.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before shell or git actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles secrets and deployment configuration in a Replit-managed cloud Repl, while Agent A is an open-source docs repo with no touched data classes. No residency or certification mismatch is evidenced in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to accidental disclosure if sensitive B data is copied into A. The other agent is not cited for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data from agent_b is copied into agent_a or public docs, THEN retention and disclosure controls may be violated.
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or certification not shown here, THEN the pair may be noncompliant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_a prompts.
Restrict agent_b secrets to the secrets store.
Review exports before publishing.
Document data-handling boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: map residency and certification requirements explicitly.
